claims.statement: Poland's GIS explains that supplements are foods rather than medicines, do not undergo clinical trials as medicines do, and should be assessed using ingredient, warning, intended-user, and usage information.

GIS maintains a public notification register and states that businesses must notify market introduction while remaining responsible for documenting food-law compliance; notification is not the same as product approval.
Hypothesis: brands and retailers will pay for a tamper-evident lot record that makes third-party laboratory evidence easy to verify and that reduces support, delisting, or trust friction.

contrary_evidence: Brands can publish certificates on their own sites, and sophisticated retailers already demand documentation directly.
A laboratory certificate only covers the tested sample and cannot prove every unit in a lot or clinical benefit.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: onboard one lab as the issuing channel, provide five free lot records to selected brands, then win retailer recognition that pulls more suppliers into the registry.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 30 brands and 500 lots in year 2, 250 brands and 8000 lots in year 4, and 700 brands across Central Europe in year 6 producing 8-14M PLN annual recurring and transaction revenue. At 3-5x revenue and 55-70% founder ownership, equity can exceed 5M PLN once lab-led distribution and retailer acceptance are repeatable.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours/week through the first lab integration, with food-law and laboratory specialists retained for bounded reviews.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 65-78% while documents receive sampled human verification, rising above 82% with lab-signed structured data.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 4-8 months at 3000-8000 PLN acquisition/onboarding cost and 1500-3500 PLN monthly blended brand revenue.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 400-900 PLN per verified lot, 499-1499 PLN/month brand workspace, and retailer API contracts.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: every manufactured lot repeats; lab integration and retailer acceptance create high switching costs and target annual net revenue retention above 110%.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Lot-by-lot supplier consistency, document authenticity, assay variance, exception, and remediation history across participating labs and brands
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish supplement brands, contract manufacturers, testing laboratories, and specialist retailers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Participating laboratories issue records directly, brands place QR codes on packaging, and retailers request BatchProof during onboarding
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Signed lot evidence page, GIS-notification link, laboratory document verification, exception workflow, QR, and retailer API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Brand pays per verified lot and monthly registry workspace; retailer or marketplace pays for status API access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new batch is released, retailer onboarding occurs, a document expires, or a consumer scans a lot code

founder_fit: Matches health, supplements, data provenance, and FMCG process interests.
Document extraction, digital signatures, anomaly detection, and supplier benchmarking fit technical skills.
B2B lab and retailer integrations avoid a founder-led influencer brand.
Can validate with public registry records and synthetic COAs before receiving private brand documents.
risks: Consumers may confuse GIS notification or a COA with safety approval or therapeutic efficacy; copy and UI must explicitly prevent that.
Forged laboratory documents and sample-selection gaming.
Adverse findings create disclosure, recall, and liability workflows requiring qualified counsel.

structure.control_point: signed lot-level evidence record linked to lab, brand, retailer, and public notification data
structure.critical_dependency: laboratory-authenticated records and retailer recognition without misleading approval claims

thesis: A lot-level provenance and verification network for independent supplement brands. It links the public GIS notification record, brand-controlled specifications, signed laboratory certificates, manufacturing lot, and retailer-facing QR/API status without claiming drug approval; repeated lots create supplier-consistency and out-of-spec benchmarks.
title: BatchProof Registry for Polish Supplements
uncertainties: Which accredited laboratories will digitally sign or verify documents through an integration is unknown.
Retailer recognition may be more valuable than consumer QR engagement but must be tested.
The 70000 PLN capital estimate and all commercial figures below are planning hypotheses.
